title: Tenses, Passive, and Reading Notices
subject: inggris
summary: Present perfect with since and for, passive voice, first conditional, text types, reported speech, and reading tone and arguments.
objectives: use since and for with the present perfect
change active sentences into the passive
recognise procedure, recount, descriptive, and narrative texts
find the tone of a text and evidence that supports a claim

sections.title: since and for
sections.html: since + a starting point: since 2019, since Monday. for + a length of time: for five years, for two days. "She has lived here since 2019."

sections.title: Passive voice
sections.html:
Passiveobject + be + past participle (+ by ...)

Active: People recycle paper. Passive: Paper is recycled. Use the passive when the action matters more than who does it.

sections.title: If it rains ...
sections.html:
First conditionalIf + present simple, will + verb

If it rains, we will stay at home. It talks about a real possibility.

sections.title: Kinds of text
sections.html: Procedure: how to make or do something (goal, materials, steps). Recount: what happened in the past. Descriptive: what a particular thing is like. Narrative: a story with a problem and a resolution. Short functional texts like notices and announcements give practical information.

sections.title: Reading between the lines
sections.html:
"Great, another rainy day," said Tom, looking at his ruined shoes. The word is positive, but the situation is not. This is sarcasm, and it shows Tom is annoyed.

Good evidence is connected to the claim. "Bicycles produce no exhaust gas" supports "cycling is good for the environment". "My bicycle is red" does not.
